references.text: In Mark's parallel account of the raising of Jairus' daughter, the parents are overcome with great astonishment, and Jesus gives them strict orders that no one should know about this.
Jesus commands the leper not to tell anyone about the healing, just as he here commands the parents to remain silent about what has happened.
Earlier in the same account, Jesus says to Jairus: 'Do not be afraid; only believe, and she will be saved.' The parents' amazement in verse 56 is their response to this promise being fulfilled.
In Matthew's parallel account of the raising of Jairus' daughter, Jesus takes the girl by the hand and raises her up, and news of this spreads throughout the region.
Jesus commands the healed leper not to say anything to anyone, but rather to go and show himself to the priest—a pattern of silence commands also found in Luke 8:56.
Jesus orders them not to tell anyone about the healing of the deaf man, a repeated pattern where Jesus seeks to limit public attention around his miraculous deeds.
Jesus strictly warns the disciples not to tell anyone that he is God's Messiah. This shows the same pattern of imposing silence as in 8:56.
Jesus heals many and commands them not to make him known, reflecting the same theme of silence found in Luke 8:56.
